summary: Federal Communications Commission urges preservation of E-Rate program to support essential broadband infrastructure for schools and libraries, citing cost implications and budget constraints. The school district argues against sunsetting E-Rate, emphasizing its importance for providing connectivity and infrastructure for modern education.

claims.argument: E-Rate has enabled schools to build necessary connectivity infrastructure
claims.evidence_quote: E-Rate has enabled schools (public and private) and libraries to build and maintain the connectivity necessary for students and patrons to participate fully in modern. As our nation seeks to prepare students for college, careers, and an increasingly technology-driven economy, now is not the time to undermine the very program and related infrastructure that makes those opportunities possible ~ particularly for districts such as mine where every school is a Title I school.
